rules.title: California Statewide Rent Cap (AB 1482 / Civ. Code § 1947.12)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot raise rent on covered residential units by more than 5% plus local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, and no more than two increases in that period.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property generally, subject to listed exemptions (deed-restricted affordable housing, dorms/schools, locally rent-controlled housing with stricter caps, housing with certificate of occupancy within prior 15 years, certain owner-occupied duplexes, and certain non-corporate single-family/condo owners with required notice).
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing; dormitories; housing subject to stricter local rent control; housing issued certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (unless mobilehome); alienable single-family/condo property owned by a non-REIT/non-corporation/non-LLC-with-corporate-member with required tenant notice; owner-occupied duplexes where owner occupies one unit.
rules.interaction: This statewide rent cap yields to stricter local rent control ordinances (e.g., Berkeley, San Francisco, Oakland, Los Angeles, Santa Ana, San Diego) covering the same units.
rules.penalty: Civil liability including injunctive relief, damages equal to overpayment, attorney's fees/costs, and treble damages for willful/oppressive/fraudulent/malicious violations; AG or city attorney/county counsel may enforce and seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.conflict_note: Sources give different effective/operative dates (March 15, 2019 original enactment; February 18, 2021 baseline amendment; April 1, 2024 current operative date); also described via Civ. Code § 827 notice provisions referencing the same statewide cap figures.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – Just Cause for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: Once all tenants have lawfully occupied a rental unit for 12 months (or at least one tenant for 24 months), a landlord must state a just cause in any notice to terminate the tenancy, and failure to comply voids the termination notice. This rule does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a more protective local ordinance adopted after that date, governs instead.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property (dwellings/units intended for human habitation, including mobilehome park units) once tenants have met the 12/24-month occupancy threshold; does not apply where a qualifying local just-cause ordinance applies instead.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to residential real property subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 (local ordinance governs), or to a more protective local ordinance adopted/amended after that date meeting specified criteria; does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome as defined in Section 798.9.
rules.interaction: Statewide just-cause requirement yields to local just-cause ordinances adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019, or stricter local ordinances adopted after that date, which apply instead.
rules.penalty: If a tenant fails to vacate after expiration of the termination notice, the relocation assistance or rent waiver amount is recoverable as damages in an action to recover possession.

rules.title: Cartwright Act Amendment - Common Pricing Algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: It is illegal to use or sell software that lets competing landlords (or other businesses) coordinate pricing by sharing nonpublic competitor data, including when used to set rents, and it is illegal to coerce someone into following the algorithm's recommended price.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person who uses or distributes a 'common pricing algorithm' (a methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term) in California; not limited to rental housing but covers it.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to proprietary algorithms using only the business's own data; does not impair other antitrust laws.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside local algorithmic pricing bans (Berkeley, San Francisco, San Diego, Santa Ana); the state law is a general antitrust prohibition applicable statewide.
rules.penalty: Criminal fines of more than $6 million for businesses and $1 million for individuals; civil fines of up to $1 million in actions brought by the Attorney General or a district attorney.
rules.quoted_span:
(a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
